# Case 08 results: propensity vs uplift targeting on the Hillstrom e-mail experiment

<!-- Generated by case-studies/08-hillstrom-email-uplift/src/run.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Reproduce (downloads ~4 MB on first run):

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python case-studies/08-hillstrom-email-uplift/src/run.py
```

Seed `20261127`. Data: Hillstrom MineThatData e-mail experiment (SHA-256 verified). 64,000 customers, randomized one third each to a men's e-mail, a women's e-mail or no e-mail; outcomes over two weeks. Intent-to-treat: treated means sent the e-mail. Scores are cross-fitted over 5 folds, so every customer is scored by models that never saw them. The propensity model is P(outcome | treated, x); the uplift model is a T-learner (treated model minus control model). Both are ridge logistic regressions on recency, log past spend, men's/women's purchase flags, new-customer flag, zip type and channel. SEs are from a 300-replicate Poisson bootstrap over customers with the ranking held fixed, so they exclude model-fitting noise. **n/e** (not estimable) marks a ratio whose denominator has a bootstrap coefficient of variation above 0.3, where the ratio's SE is not meaningful; with about 212 incremental conversions from sending any e-mail, most conversion ratios are n/e.

| Any e-mail | conversion | 0.0057 | 0.0107 | +0.0050 (0.0007) | +86.5% |
| Men's e-mail | visit | 0.1062 | 0.1828 | +0.0766 (0.0034) | +72.1% |
| Men's e-mail | conversion | 0.0057 | 0.0125 | +0.0068 (0.0009) | +118.8% |
| Women's e-mail | visit | 0.1062 | 0.1514 | +0.0452 (0.0032) | +42.6% |
| Women's e-mail | conversion | 0.0057 | 0.0088 | +0.0031 (0.0008) | +54.3% |
